dossier.architecture: Light articulated intake and adjustable shooter, with one-shot ratcheting chain engagement.

subsystems.drivetrain: Low-central electrical packaging intended to protect center of gravity and resist note trapping.
subsystems.intake: Multi-roller polycarbonate collector with grip tape and reinforcing shafts.
subsystems.transfer: Bent note path feeds the launcher; sensors select amp versus shooter routing.
subsystems.scoring: Adjustable launcher, automatic angle/speed selection; interview reports roughly 17–65-degree motion.
subsystems.endgame: Ratcheting hooks deploy and latch in a one-shot action; cannot simply reset on field.
subsystems.controls: Angled Limelights/MegaTag2, gyro and module odometry; automatic pickup, aim and amp alignment.

versions: Interview describes competition package; detailed sequence of earlier builds is not given.
dossier.analysis: A one-shot endgame can reduce driver actions while losing recovery flexibility. That tradeoff belongs in architecture selection and reliability assessment.
limits: Intermediate undocumented changes are not inferred; specifications and plans retain their source context.

context_documents.title: 2024-9483 · A broad angle range needs controlled note position and a fallback pose estimate
context_documents.body:
# 2024-9483: A broad angle range needs controlled note position and a fallback pose estimate

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Six collector rollers, gripping wrap and reinforced polycarbonate feed a bent note path. Sensors distinguish staging and the amp/shooter route. The interview reports an adjustable launch range approximately 17–65 degrees with automatic speed/angle selection; pose estimation continues through brief vision loss.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source connects grip material to acquisition and center-mounted/protected hardware to avoiding collision interruption. Exact optimum compression and a complete field range envelope are not established by the passage.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A numerical angle range is a mechanical envelope, not a guarantee that every field position is accurate. Flexible notes arrive with different deformation and velocity, while pose confidence may degrade during occlusion. The appropriate architecture includes a readiness condition and safe fallback, not just an interpolation table.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure staged pose, accuracy versus range/angle, and performance after controlled vision dropout. Verify actual angular limits in code or CAD before reusing the caption numbers.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/GaLm00wcnVE](https://youtu.be/GaLm00wcnVE)

source_reviews.title: Team 9483 Robots
source_reviews.review_basis: Team publication read; separately inspected full-resolution portrait.
facts: Identifies Snapfire and records the Bosphorus and Marmara regional wins and Milstein division win.
source_reviews.limitations: Season summary gives results; the portrait supplies geometry at one pose.

source_reviews.title: Snapfire team portrait
source_reviews.locator: Central roller stack and side plates above numbered bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Direct visual review of team photograph.
facts: Two thick, spaced roller contact regions per shaft across two prominent levels; multiple narrower transverse rollers behind and above; side pulley/belt and chain elements visible.
source_reviews.limitations: Exterior only. Dark areas, overlapping hardware and one parked pose prevent a complete part or transmission count.

source_reviews.title: FIRST Updates Now 9483 interview announcement photographs
source_reviews.review_basis: Direct visual review of two published photos, cross-checked against team portrait.
facts: Orange note visible among the roller structures, above clear panels; lower front module hardware and two inclined bars visible.
source_reviews.limitations: Still photos have no sequence or electrical identification. The linked interview captions returned HTTP 429 and interview content was unavailable.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Snapfire packages several levels of note-contact hardware into a tall assembly over a low drivebase. The team portrait establishes the separation between a wide upper roller assembly and larger paired contact surfaces facing out from a lower level. The pit photograph shows that an actual note can occupy the intervening volume. The architecture is best read as linked acquisition, controlled transport and launch problems: each interface must keep the note supported until the next contact takes over. The visible stack and protected deck are stronger evidence than any specific automatic scoring sequence.
source_review.piece_flow: The reviewed stills establish a note position inside the upper/central mechanism and show the clear deck beneath it. They cannot establish which shafts run during that state or whether the note is staged there for Amp or Speaker. The corpus associates the upper assembly with articulated pickup and a bent transfer, then sensor-based staging and selection between Amp and shooter. Those are prior leads for verification. Mechanically, a bent path must control the rim at the entrance and at the last driven nip so that incoming orientation does not dictate exit orientation.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The portrait puts the main moving assemblies above the bumper line, with metal drive hardware still visible low at the corners. Long inclined members bracket the roller area from the frame up to the vertical structure. Their fixed geometry in both stills constrains the space available to a swinging arm or roller group. The clear panels shown from above lie close to the deck; they also keep loose objects and notes away from parts of the lower bay if the edges remain covered. Hinge axes, travel and electronics locations require different views.

subsystems.name: Collector and transfer
subsystems.construction: Several transverse rollers are visible in the upper assembly; the pit image exposes clear side material and a white transverse roller near the note.
subsystems.operation: Visible contacts give the ring successive surfaces along its width. Its direction through them and which are driven are unresolved in the stills.
subsystems.team_rationale: No collector design rationale in the reviewed team season text.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Spanning the note width gives room for an off-center capture, but a flexible ring can cock if one rim reaches the next nip first. Compression should be measured with the arm loaded.
subsystems.interfaces: Outer roller to inner roller, then the clear guide and the launcher throat; guide edge height controls whether the leading rim dives below the next contact.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect guide edges and roller traction after impacts. Witness marks on one guide wall can reveal a biased feed before it becomes a jam.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller count, material, deployment geometry and drive routing from the old synopsis remain unconfirmed.

subsystems.name: Launcher and angular positioning
subsystems.construction: Two conspicuous upper/lower shafts carry paired, thick, textured contact bands. Side drive elements are visible beside the roller assembly.
subsystems.operation: An opposing contact pair can compress and accelerate a ring. The side transmission is visible, but exact rotation direction and assignment of each drive element remain unknown.
subsystems.team_rationale: The reviewed primary photo supplies geometry only.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A split left/right contact surface can feed a flexible ring asymmetrically if it is off center; check exit yaw and speed at multiple lateral offsets before adjusting a range map.
subsystems.interfaces: The upstream note position defines first contact; the frame-side transmission and its supports define how repeatably the exit direction can be held.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare physical release direction with commanded angle after side transmission service, especially at opposite ends of travel.
subsystems.unknowns: Pivot range, feedback, wheel speeds, and ready-to-fire logic require primary verification.

subsystems.name: Base and endgame packaging
subsystems.construction: The portrait shows front corner drive hardware below the roller frame, inclined supports and two upright side structures.
subsystems.operation: Drive hardware carries the moving upper assembly. Endgame engagement sequence is unresolved by these sources.
subsystems.team_rationale: No endgame rationale in the reviewed team publication.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Pitch and chassis roll alter the world-space exit angle and would also change the approach of a chain hook.
subsystems.interfaces: Corner modules, upright bases and the swing envelope share the same bounded chassis volume.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check bumper access and wiring strain after moving the upper structure through its full travel.
subsystems.unknowns: A one-shot ratchet is a corpus lead only; its load path, reset and release are unverified.

revisions: The team page and the interview announcement document a Championship configuration and result. Neither dates component changes.
transferable_principles: Pair an exterior photo with a loaded side view to establish which surfaces actually constrain the note.
Measure the launcher’s exit distribution across staged note offsets and note wear.
disconfirming_conditions: A staged note seen in a photo could be manually placed.
Separate scoring paths or passive shafts would change the inferred functional division.
remaining_gaps: Interview content, roller and chain kinematics, Amp routing, sensor identities, pose fallback and climb load path remain open.

recommended_images.subject: Complete stowed geometry and roller contact bands
Loaded note and clear deck close-up
